phase3_findings.description: outgoing_query_info returns the caller's own dict when no guard applies; internal and outgoing query shapes are both plain dicts, so the outgoing-only invariant rests on convention.
has_rewriting_guard mirrors factory.py wiring conditions rather than asking which guards were wired; the Markdown and metadata labels are decided at two call sites.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (two Important checklist failures: absolute "never shown" claims in the external docs)

The PR is not ready to merge: two doc lines it adds say the rewritten SQL is never shown, but a database error can still quote fragments of the rewritten statement back to the client.

Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-8: FAIL (important) — The rewritten SQL is never shown to the client on any rail (Markdown, sqllens/query, agent trace, error results) [docs/external/row-level-security.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/external/row-level-security.md:125 says 'The rewritten statement is never shown to the client.' The success-path SQL rails use the as-written SQL (query_database.py:525-562 _as_written_sql / outgoing_query_info). The error rails do not. RlsGuardRunner.run_sql (safety/__init__.py:195-234) passes the rewritten SQL to the inner runner. The MySQL runner (agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py) has no except that sanitizes, and its docstring line 98 says pymysql.Error propagates. run_sql.py:211-226 then builds 'Error executing query: {str(e)}' into result_for_llm, the error NotificationComponent message and ToolResult.error. _format.py:384-387 returns that card description as error_message, which becomes the 'SQL execution error: ' client error (query_database.py:936). _format.py:712-715 and 755-756 put the same text verbatim in the agent trace step error and terminal_error. _format.py:721-725 states these are deliberately not scrubbed. MySQL server errors such as 'You have an error in your SQL syntax ... near ...' and 'Unknown column ...' quote fragments of the executed (rewritten) statement. Because the executed statement is the rewritten one, those fragments can include the injected predicate, so the rewritten SQL text can reach the client through error results and the agent trace. Counterexample input: an [[rls]] query that passes the guard but fails at MySQL. The absolute claim 'never shown' is therefore false for error results and trace. Caveat: I did not run MySQL, so the exact error text is from known driver behavior, not from a run.

  </details>

- VC-9: FAIL (important) — The rewritten SQL under a rule set is never shown [docs/external/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/external/rule-sets.md:300 says 'The rewritten SQL is never shown' (absolute). The show_details block does use the as-written SQL (query_database.py:940), but the rewritten SQL can still reach the client/agent through a database error. RuleSetGuardRunner passes the rewritten SQL to the inner runner (rule_sets.py:894-896). RefusalRedactingRunner only redacts UnsafeSqlError/RlsError and its docstring says 'Database errors pass through unchanged' (rule_sets.py:983-1016). mysql/sql_runner.py comments (lines 178-180) say the primary query error reaches the LLM intact. agent/tools/run_sql.py:211-225 turns the exception into 'Error executing query: {str(e)}' as result_for_llm, a UI component and error=str(e). agent/integrations/sql_threads.py:37-38 itself notes the exception message 'can quote the SQL'. A MySQL syntax error ('near ...') or an unknown-table error on a rewritten derived table or link table therefore shows rewritten SQL fragments or link-table names. Query_database.py:934-936 then raises 'SQL execution error: {answer}' to the caller. So 'never' is not true for DB error text. I did not run MySQL; this rests on reading the pass-through path.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `outgoing_query_info` in src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py returns the caller's own dict when no guard applies, and the internal and outgoing query shapes are both plain dicts, so the outgoing-only invariant rests on convention (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `has_rewriting_guard` in src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py mirrors factory.py's wiring conditions instead of asking which guards were wired, and the Markdown and metadata labels are decided at two call sites (raised by 1/6 agents)

- VC-19: FAIL (suggestion) — The query_database docstring says the default profile keeps show_details off so the SQL block is suppressed. [src/sqllens/server.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  server.py:461-462 docstring says the default profile keeps show_details off so the SQL block is suppressed. profiles.py:301-310 resolve_effective_settings: with no profile, name=default; the default profile (or an empty Profile()) has show_details=None, which inherits cfg.agent.show_details. With cfg.agent.show_details=true and no profile selected, show_details resolves true, and query_database.py:899-906 then attaches SQL/trace. The default profile can also set show_details=true explicitly. So the docstring is false in that case; the same docstring (server.py:446) says default 'falls back to base config'. The line is unchanged context in the diff (diff.patch:275-276), not added by the PR.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (1)

<details><summary>1 item</summary>

- VC-6: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — sqllens verify-memory compares the agent's SQL with golden SQL through sqlglot, and sqlglot keeps comments (so a note line would change the comparison) [docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo half verified: src/sqllens/eval/runner.py:152 calls compare_sql(expected, actual, dialect=...), and src/sqllens/eval/compare.py:39-72 normalizes both sides via sqlglot.parse(...) then statement.sql(dialect=..., normalize=True, pretty=False) and compares strings. Nothing in compare.py strips comments or passes comments=False, so whether a note line changes the comparison depends solely on sqlglot's parser/generator keeping comments. No dependency_sources were supplied and sqlglot source is not in the views, so that library behavior could not be read. Missing evidence: sqlglot's parser comment attachment and Generator comments default (not read). No test in the repo's compare tests exercises comments either.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The **note line** is exactly `-- SQL Lens applies this server's access rules to queries before running them, so the query that ran can differ from this text.` The outgoing SQL described in the criteria below, `docs/external/rule-sets.md`, `docs/external/configuration.md` and `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` each carry it verbatim.
- [ ] On a server whose config loads a rule-set file, and on a server with at least one `[[rls]]` rule and no rule-set file, for a successful `query_database` answer that ran SQL with `show_details` on, the Markdown that `query_database_impl_with_widgets` returns ends with `**Query as written:**` followed by a fenced `sql` block whose first line is the note line and whose remaining lines are the model's SQL exactly. The tool result's text content carries that Markdown unchanged, followed only by the conversation-ID footer when `agent.show_conversation_footer` is on.
- [ ] In the same two cases, `_meta["sqllens/query"]` has `sql` equal to the note line, a newline and the model's SQL, and `"as_written": true`. Its `query_type` is computed from the model's SQL without the note line, and its `row_count` is the number of rows the query returned, both as before the change.
- [ ] On a server with no rule-set file and no `[[rls]]` rules, the Markdown answer and `_meta["sqllens/query"]` are byte-for-byte what they are before the change: the `**Executed SQL:**` heading, no note line and no `as_written` key.
- [ ] On a server with a rule-set file or at least one `[[rls]]` rule, an answer with `show_details` off carries no SQL block, no note line and no `sqllens/query` key, and a failed turn's error result carries no `sqllens/query` key.
- [ ] On a server with a rule-set file or at least one `[[rls]]` rule, the `query_info` that `query_database_impl_with_widgets` returns, and the `query_info` on an `AgentRunError` it raises, hold the model's SQL with no note line, so `sqllens verify-memory` on a flat-RLS server compares the same SQL as before the change.
- [ ] Under a rule set whose queried table has a row rule, and under an `[[rls]]` rule on a table the query reads, neither the Markdown answer nor `_meta["sqllens/query"]` contains the SQL text the guard passed to the runner beneath it, and neither contains the predicate the guard added.
- [ ] The change leaves `_meta["sqllens/agent_trace"]` unchanged: a `run_sql` step's `arguments.sql` is the model's SQL with no note line.
- [ ] `docs/external/rule-sets.md`'s Limits bullet about `show_details` states that the SQL appears under `**Query as written:**`, starts with the note line, carries `as_written: true` in `sqllens/query`, and is the SQL the model wrote before the guard's rewrite, not the SQL MySQL ran.
- [ ] `docs/external/configuration.md`'s `show_details` row states that on a server with a rule-set file or `[[rls]]` rules the heading is `**Query as written:**`, the SQL starts with the note line, and `sqllens/query` carries `as_written: true`. The row no longer calls the shown SQL "the SQL the agent executed" or "the executed SQL"; it calls it the SQL the agent wrote.
- [ ] `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md`'s Executed SQL channel section states the behavior on a server with a rule-set file or `[[rls]]` rules, documents `as_written` and the note line as parts of the outgoing `_meta["sqllens/query"]` value only, and states that the `query_info` dict `query_database_impl_with_widgets` returns keeps its documented `{"sql", "query_type", "row_count"?}` shape with the model's SQL and no note line.
- [ ] The `query_database` MCP tool description in `src/sqllens/server.py` states that on a server with a rule-set file or `[[rls]]` rules the SQL is the query as written and starts with the note line, and it no longer says the result widget renders the SQL.
- [ ] After the change, no line that `git grep -n -i -P 'executed[ _-]?sql' -- src docs/internal docs/external ':!docs/external/release-notes.md'` finds calls the SQL in the Markdown block, in `_meta["sqllens/query"].sql` or in the `query_info` that `query_database_impl_with_widgets` returns "the executed SQL" or the SQL that ran, unless the line limits that to servers with no rule-set file and no `[[rls]]` rules. Lines that only name the removed in-widget "Executed SQL" panel, the `run_sql` status card, or `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md`'s "Executed SQL channel" section and its anchor are not such lines and may stay as they are.
